TestDistributedTTL::test_ttl_is_replicat.description: 2-node cluster, RF=2 (NTS), table default_time_to_live=5. Inserts a row at CL=ALL, reads ttl(col1) via exclusive connections to node1 and node2 and asserts the remaining TTLs differ by <=1s, then sleeps 7s and asserts the row is gone at CL=ALL. Guards that the default TTL is applied to the mutation and replicated with it, not recomputed per replica.

TestDistributedTTL::test_ttl_is_replicat.reason: Basic multi-node TTL replication; no scylla cluster test checks per-replica TTL, but the assertion is weak: reads use CL=ONE via exclusive connections (ttl_test.py:683-684), so each coordinator usually reads its local replica but this is not guaranteed, and the check is only |ttl1-ttl2|<=1. Cheap (17s) but low-value; second opinion.

issues.text: CL=ONE exclusive-connection reads may not hit the local replica, and |ttl1-ttl2|<=1 can't detect per-replica TTL recomputation.

TestDistributedTTL::test_ttl_is_respecte.description: 2 nodes RF=2, shadow_round_ms=1000. Stops node2, writes key1 TTL 5 and key2 TTL 1000 to node1 (CL=ONE, hints stored), waits for key1 to expire, stops node1, starts node2 (expects empty), restarts node1 (hint replay), runs cleanup, then asserts at CL=ALL from node2 that only key2 exists and that ttl(col1) on both nodes matches within 1s. Guards that expired data is not resurrected by hinted handoff / read repair and that replayed hints keep the original expiry.
